Subject: Security + KMS questions - follow-up from today

Hi Olivia / Marcus -

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap + next steps from our side and a few clarifying questions on encryption/key management for your security team so we can prepare the vendor questionnaire: 

Summary from the call:
- Demo covered hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment options.
- Discussed SLAs, throughput needs, and data residency.
- FinBank expressed interest in customer-managed keys (CMK) for sensitive workloads and asked about SOC 2 and GDPR/HIPAA posture.

Questions for your security team (short list):
1) For production workloads, do you require customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption, or is provider-managed KMS acceptable for non-PHI workloads?
2) If CMK required: do you prefer AWS KMS (Cloud KMS) integrations or an HSM-backed on-prem solution?
3) Any specific requirements around HSM certs / FIPS / PCI underwriting we should be aware of?

What I attached: vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx (blank), redwood-kms-architecture-diagram.pdf (high-level).

Quick answers to expect from our side - we can produce a more formal answer in the questionnaire:
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS optional for Private deployments.
- Data at rest: encrypted using KMS-managed keys by default; we support BYOK/CMK for hosted and Dedicated via AWS KMS integrations. Private deployments can be configured to use customer-controlled HSMs.
- SOC 2: we have a SOC 2 Type II report; happy to share the artifact under an NDA / secure link.

Next steps I propose:
- Olivia: confirm whether CMK is required and which KMS/HSM option you prefer.
- Once we have that, we'll return the completed questionnaire and set up a technical deep-dive with our security engineer (Rishi) to go over key rotation, audit logs, and KMS access controls.

Available times for a 45-min tech call next week: Tue/Wed 9-12 PT, Thu 1-4 PT.

Thanks -
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Naomi -

Thanks for the recap and attachments. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we kick off the questionnaire: 

1) For our regulated workloads we do require customer-managed keys for data at rest (BYOK). Provider-managed keys are acceptable for lower-risk dev/test environments only.
2) Our preference is to use AWS KMS (CloudHSM for keys that require HSM-backed protection). We have an existing AWS CloudHSM estate in us-west-2.
3) SOC 2: we will need to review your SOC 2 Type II report. Please provide a secure link or indicate if you prefer to share under an NDA.

Also: please include details on key rotation policies, key access audit logs, and whether Redwood stores plaintext keys at any point.

I can coordinate the technical call - Tue/Wed next week looks good.

Best,
Olivia Grant

Hi Olivia -

Great, thanks for the clarity. I've also attached a short one-page KMS summary and the questionnaire we filled out for your team.

Quick answers:
- Do we support BYOK/CMK? Yes. For hosted (Redwood API) customers we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (customer grants us a key policy/role to encrypt/decrypt). For Dedicated capacity, we offer the same AWS KMS integration and can also support bringing your own CloudHSM-protected keys if required. For Private deployments we support integrations to your HSMs and can run within your VPC/air-gapped environment where keys never leave your control.
- Do we store plaintext keys? No - Redwood never stores plaintext customer keys. We store encrypted key references / key IDs and use KMS/HSM APIs to perform cryptographic operations.
- Key rotation & audit logs: We support key rotation as configured in your KMS and surface KMS events in our audit logs. We can export detailed KMS access logs and provide audit evidence for key usage tied to request ids and timestamps.
- In-transit encryption: TLS 1.2+ by default; mTLS available for Private deployments and selected Dedicated integrations.

SOC 2: Our most recent SOC 2 Type II report is available at the link below (protected). If you need a signed copy we can provide it via DocuSign/secure transfer after a quick NDA.

Attachments: vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx (completed v0.5), redwood-kms-onepager.pdf (summary), redwood-kms-architecture-diagram.pdf
Links: https://drive.google.com/redwood/soc2-report-2025.pdf

- Rishi (cc'd) will join the technical call to review integration patterns and confirm configuration steps for AWS KMS/CloudHSM.
